headline: Would have canceled a Labor Department rule letting retirement plan managers consider climate and other ESG factors when investing.
what_it_does: This resolution would have overturned a Department of Labor rule issued on December 1, 2022. That rule says people who manage employee benefit plans, such as workplace retirement plans, may consider climate change and other environmental, social, and governance (ESG) factors when choosing investments. The rule also allows them to consider these factors when using shareholder rights, like voting on shareholder proposals and board nominees. Congress passed the resolution, but the President vetoed it, and the House failed to override the veto on March 23, 2023.

who_it_affects.group: Managers and fiduciaries of workplace retirement and benefit plans
who_it_affects.how: They would have lost the rule's clear permission to weigh climate and other ESG factors in investment choices and shareholder votes.

who_it_affects.group: Workers and retirees with employer-sponsored retirement plans
who_it_affects.how: The rules guiding how their plan savings are invested and how their plan votes as a shareholder would have changed.

who_it_affects.group: Companies whose stock is held by benefit plans
who_it_affects.how: Shareholder votes cast by plan managers on proposals and board nominations could have been decided under different standards.
